claims.text: An interfacial CrN layer will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion between the elemental Cr coating and zirconium-alloy substrate.
Reducing Cr–Zr interdiffusion with CrN will extend the durability of the elemental Cr coating.
The CrN-modified coating will retain improved oxidation resistance in subcritical water at approximately 300°C.
The CrN-modified coating will retain improved oxidation resistance in high-temperature steam above 1000°C.
A thin CrN layer can be engineered at the interface between the elemental Cr coating and zirconium-alloy substrate.
Limiting interfacial Cr and Zr transport will preserve the coating's mechanical integrity.
Limiting interfacial Cr and Zr transport will preserve the coating's oxidation resistance.
Relative to a Cr coating applied directly to zirconium alloy, the CrN-containing coating will exhibit less interfacial Cr–Zr transport.
Relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the CrN-containing coating will exhibit better resistance to spallation, delamination, or other integrity loss.
Relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the CrN-containing coating will exhibit better oxidation behavior.
Initial evidence supports CrN barriers as effective for limiting interdiffusion and preserving oxidation resistance.
The long-term stability of the CrN-containing coating under cyclic thermal stress is uncertain.
The stability of the CrN-containing coating under reactor-specific radiation is uncertain.
